Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund, distributed automatically using Brightline’s records. Fees and expenses would be paid separately, subject to court approval; any amount not awarded would go to the class. We’re ready to discuss the numbers, but direct payment to members is important.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that direct, automatic payments using Brightline’s records are the right approach. We can offer a $28 million class fund plus $5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your agreement on automatic distribution and on directing any unawarded fees to the class. To narrow the gap, we can move to a $30 million class fund and $6 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with the other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement and agree on automatic payments and directing any unawarded fees to the class. To continue closing the gap, we propose a $29 million class fund and $5.5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with the remaining terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We’re close. To resolve the remaining gap, we propose a $29.5 million class fund and $5.75 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Payments would remain automatic, and any fees not awarded would go to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We’re very close. We can resolve this at a $29.25 million class fund and $5.625 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Payments remain automatic, and any unawarded fees go to the class. There would be no clear-sailing provision.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept your latest term sheet: a $29.25 million class fund with automatic payments, $5.625 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class. We look forward to documenting the agreement for court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery while leaving room to negotiate. Automatic distribution is feasible and avoids the reduced payouts of a claims process. Keep any unawarded fees with the class and avoid a clear-sailing provision.

The $39 million proposal is within authority and has court-friendly distribution terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Counter with automatic payments and no fee reversion, preserving approval prospects.
The defense offer provides automatic payments and a substantial class recovery. There is room to negotiate a higher fund while preserving the agreed distribution and fee protections.
The $36 million offer is within authority and uses court-favorable terms, but there is time to seek a modest reduction without changing the agreed distribution protections.

The remaining gap is modest. A midpoint proposal improves the class recovery while preserving automatic distribution and directing any unawarded fees to members. Fees remain subject to court approval.

Their $35.25 million proposal is within authorization and has court-approval-friendly terms. A modest counteroffer may reduce Brightline's outlay without materially jeopardizing settlement; their current offer remains available to accept if needed.

The $29.25 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million trial-value estimate before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The separately paid fee is subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class. Accepting serves the class's interests.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). Counsel exchanged proposals over three rounds before accepting Brightline’s final offer in the fourth. From the first proposal, the parties discussed both class relief and attorneys’ fees; fees were not deferred until after class relief was agreed. Throughout the negotiations, we sought automatic payments to identified members and agreed that any fees not awarded by the court would go to the class. The parties moved from initial proposals of a $32 million class fund and $7 million in fees, and a $28 million class fund and $5 million in fees, to a binding agreement providing a $29.25 million class fund and $5.625 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. There is no clear-sailing provision. The fee is paid separately from the class fund, and any unawarded portion will benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline.
